stories.headline: Empty Convoy fails its post-fix gameplay sign-off despite passing focused tests
stories.summary: A post-land manual check did not accept the Empty Convoy encounter correction. The Operator reached the prepared approach point, but the reviewer reported a possible scenario mismatch; the exact cause remains unknown. A separate documented QA checkout was safely retired, with host-reported disk recovery. Independent review remains outstanding.
stories.body: The security correction was previously landed and passed targeted headless tests. The subsequent authorized GUI check reached its prepared approach, but the human reviewer returned NOT_ACCEPTED and reported a possible encounter mismatch. No successful defense, custody trace or exactly-once salvage was confirmed. The post-land closeout receipt reports scoped evidence preservation and non-forced removal of one detached QA worktree, with disk free increasing by about 6.92 GiB. These are documented host observations, not independently remeasured by WIRE. The original gameplay failure is unresolved; no paired review PASS is established. Main also contains a subsequent whitespace-only receipt edit.

article.lead: Empty Convoy's security correction has met its first significant post-land obstacle: the human gameplay check did not accept it. The Operator reached the prepared encounter approach, but the reviewer still could not confirm that the intended scenario behaved correctly. Passing focused tests has not yet translated into a successful player-facing encounter.

sections.heading: The test reached the site, not the finish line
sections.text: The documented GUI run positioned the Operator for a manual check. The reviewer returned a possible scenario or encounter mismatch. No confirmed defender battle, custody trace or one-time salvage result followed, leaving the original failure unexplained.

sections.heading: Cleanup succeeded on a narrower evidentiary footing
sections.text: The closeout record describes preservation of QA evidence, scoped cleanup and ordinary removal of a detached checkout. It reports one fewer attached worktree and about 6.92 GiB more free disk. WIRE has not independently inspected the host, so these are source-reported measurements, not live telemetry.

insights.title: A passing security test can miss a scenario mismatch
insights.explanation: The correction guards against treating failed enemy spawns as victory, but the manual outcome suggests the remaining problem may involve reaching or identifying the intended encounter. That possibility needs diagnosis, not an assumed fix.

insights.title: A closed QA checkout does not close the gameplay issue
insights.explanation: The temporary test environment can be retired while the correction remains unaccepted. Cleanup and gameplay acceptance are distinct gates.

article.takeaway: The fix is landed and test-backed, but the player-facing Empty Convoy outcome is not accepted; the root cause remains unconfirmed.
article.next_watch: A source-bound diagnosis of the manual scenario mismatch, a fresh integrated retest and a separate independent review disposition.

stories.headline: CUSTODIAN rewrites its environmental storytelling rules: every ruin needs a real history
stories.summary: New design guidance on main requires procedural locations to have a specific causal history before clues are placed. Ordinary labor, repairs and consequences take priority over interchangeable contradictory logs and manufactured mysteries. This is an authoring-standard change, not a runtime generator update.
stories.body: The newly landed design revision asks authors to define a site's original purpose, responsible people, consequential decision or failure, material cost and surviving traces before constructing clues. The Refused Passage, machine shelter and rare False Seam examples were revised to make physical consequences legible. Continuity anomalies remain exceptional and must be grounded in compatible metadata and corroborating physical evidence. This updates design doctrine only: it does not demonstrate changed generated maps, assets, runtime payloads or gameplay. The next meaningful gate is a source-bound content implementation and visual/interactive evaluation against these rules.
bullets: Causal local history now precedes procedural clue placement.
Ordinary maintenance, scarcity and human consequences are preferred over default contradictions.
Rare continuity anomalies require physical corroboration and compatible canon.
No runtime generator implementation or gameplay validation is established.

article.lead: A new design rule changes how CUSTODIAN's world should tell stories. Instead of scattering ominous records around ruins and leaving the cause undefined, every substantial location must begin with an actual event: who built it, what happened there, what it cost, and what the player can still see.

sections.heading: The world must have a past before it has clues
sections.text: The revised authoring guidance requires a specific chain of cause and effect before environmental props or inspection text are selected. Repairs, salvaged machinery, abandoned routes and lived-in shelters can tell complete stories without requiring a supernatural twist.

sections.heading: Anomalies become rare exceptions, not reusable templates
sections.text: The Refused Passage now needs an authored closure motive and human cost. The machine shelter needs an identifiable resource constraint. The False Seam can still suggest an extraordinary continuity event, but only where physical evidence and established lore support it. Contradictory paperwork alone is no longer enough.

sections.heading: This is design direction, not shipped procedural behavior
sections.text: The change is confined to documentation and authoring standards. It does not prove the procedural generator selects coherent histories, that new artwork exists, or that players can discover the intended consequences in-game.

insights.title: A mystery is stronger when the author knows its answer
insights.explanation: Requiring a real underlying event makes clues mutually consistent and lets discoveries resolve something concrete, rather than treating ambiguity as a substitute for worldbuilding.

insights.title: Ordinary lives can carry the setting
insights.explanation: Maintenance, scarcity, adaptation and institutional choices now have explicit priority. This broadens environmental variety while reserving genuine continuity anomalies for places where they matter.

article.takeaway: The design standard now favors causally coherent, materially legible environmental storytelling; runtime adoption remains unverified.
article.next_watch: A concrete procedural-location implementation, authored sample or integrated map test demonstrating these standards.

stories.headline: Empty Convoy security fix lands; a full gameplay retest still stands between code and confidence
stories.summary: The Empty Convoy correction has landed on main after focused security, recovery and placement tests passed. Temporary spawn failures now keep the encounter unresolved rather than granting the custody trace. The original production trigger is still unknown, and neither an integrated GUI retest nor independent review is accepted.
stories.body: A targeted correction to Empty Convoy's defense state machine is now on main. Temporary ambient-capacity exhaustion, unsafe spawn positions, queue rejection and missing actors on reentry no longer count as an empty or defeated defense. The trace requires verified defender defeats or authoritative absence. The archived implementation packet reports focused security, recovery and placement smokes passing, including a generated-map seed-2 scenario that registered three defenders; canonical changed-file validation reported 4/4 passing. This is implementation and source-bound test evidence, not a new production gameplay PASS. The original trigger remains unknown; a coordinator-directed GUI retest and separate review decision remain outstanding. No host teardown or live-process state was verified.

article.lead: Empty Convoy's defense loophole has received a targeted fix. Previously, temporary failures to produce enemies could leave the site looking cleared and allow the player to record the missing shipment's custody trace without a fight. The new implementation keeps that security state unresolved until the encounter has trustworthy evidence of clearance.

sections.heading: The encounter now distinguishes failure from victory
sections.text: Capacity limits, rejected spawn positions, failed queues and enemies missing after reentry no longer masquerade as a defeated defense. The trace opens only after verified defeats or a genuinely authoritative empty-defense result. This protects the event's salvage reward without changing its larger design.

sections.heading: Tests passed, but the original gameplay failure needs another look
sections.text: The implementation packet reports passing security, recovery and placement smoke tests. A generated seed-2 map accepted three registered defenders, and the changed-file validation reported four passing checks. However, the exact cause of the original in-game failure remains unknown. A new production GUI retest and an independent review decision are still needed.

insights.title: Security state must follow evidence, not absence
insights.explanation: No enemies visible is not the same as enemies defeated. This distinction protects both the encounter and its exactly-once salvage reward against temporary world-generation or spawning failures.

insights.title: A headless PASS is not a gameplay PASS
insights.explanation: The corrected source passed targeted tests, but only a fresh integrated retest can establish that the originally observed player-facing bypass is gone.

article.takeaway: The correction is landed and test-backed, but its player-facing resolution is not yet independently established.
article.next_watch: A coordinator-directed production seed-2 GUI retest, followed by a separate review disposition.

stories.body: A documented integrated gameplay retest on contract seed 2 (generated map seed 3570245418) found no hostiles after scanning the cargo cradle, yet RECORD CUSTODY TRACE appeared immediately. Source inspection in the newly committed packet identifies several ways temporary spawn or observation failures can become empty_defense, which the recovery step treats as clearance. The exact trigger in that run remains unknown. The new P1 packet is ready/auto in source, not proven claimed or running. It requires deferred retry, authoritative defeat evidence, safe reentry, and production-realistic regression tests before any corrected behavior can be claimed. C1-C3 implementations remain landed; their waived reviews do not establish independent acceptance.

article.lead: The Empty Convoy's new encounter has an important gap: in an integrated retest, its defenders never appeared, but the player was allowed to record the shipment's custody trace anyway. A targeted correction has now been queued, not yet implemented.

sections.heading: When no enemies appear, the game assumes the fight is over
sections.text: The documented retest reached the cargo cradle without seeing hostiles, then immediately offered RECORD CUSTODY TRACE. The newly authored correction packet identifies multiple paths where a temporary failure to spawn or track defenders can be mistaken for a legitimately empty defense.

sections.heading: A narrow fix instead of another encounter rewrite
sections.text: The P1 correction calls for retrying temporary failures, preserving unresolved security on reentry, and requiring authoritative enemy defeat before allowing the trace or salvage. It also calls for realistic navigation and queue-failure tests. The exact cause of the observed run is still unconfirmed.

insights.title: A graceful fallback became an unintended shortcut
insights.explanation: The safe-empty outcome protects against genuinely absent defenders, but it must not also treat capacity or navigation failures as completed combat. That distinction controls whether the player's evidence and salvage are earned.

insights.title: Focused tests missed an integrated state transition
insights.explanation: Earlier selected tests were reported passing, yet the integrated retest found a player-facing failure. The new validation must exercise real spawning and walkability behavior, not only simplified probes.

article.takeaway: The failure is documented and a correction packet exists; no corrected runtime behavior or independent acceptance has yet been verified.
article.next_watch: Watch for the correction implementation, focused realistic regressions, and a separately decided review disposition.

stories.headline: Empty Convoy's missing shipment can now be traced, but its reviews remain waived
stories.summary: The Empty Convoy encounter gained bounded security and a one-time custody trace with optional salvage. Its three implementation slices landed, while security and recovery independent reviews were owner-waived before launch. The latest recovery review hit a source-attestation gate, not a gameplay verdict.
stories.body: The Empty Convoy encounter progressed beyond optional placement. Security scanning now queues up to three registered enemies within ambient spawn capacity and fails safely when placement is impossible. After clearing security, the player can record an unverified shipment trace and obtain existing ruin_scrap once when the ledger supports it; otherwise evidence-only completion is preserved. C2 landed at bde08b88 and C3 at e346eaea. C2 implementation reports 10/10 selected validation checks, C3 reports 8/8. The C2 review was owner-waived without launch. C3 review was also waived before launch after the host gate rejected missing authenticated source-span provenance for the changed validation manifest. No independent PASS, gameplay acceptance or verified host teardown follows from these commits.

article.lead: The abandoned convoy now offers more than an eerie roadside discovery. Scanning its cargo cradle can trigger a contained defense, and surviving the encounter reveals a custody trace that refuses to pretend the missing shipment has been found. The code landed, but neither follow-up slice received independent review.

sections.heading: A threat that respects the rest of the world
sections.text: The scan queues at most three existing security units, sharing the game's ambient enemy capacity rather than creating an unlimited separate wave. If safe spawning fails, the event falls back to evidence instead of trapping the player or crashing.

sections.heading: One clue, one salvage opportunity
sections.text: After security clears, the convoy records SHIPMENT UNVERIFIED. A valid existing scrap reward may be granted once; repeated interactions and same-run reentry cannot duplicate it. Without a usable ledger entry, the clue still remains accessible.

sections.heading: The missing verdict
sections.text: Both security and recovery implementation packets landed with reported focused checks. Their paired reviews were waived before a reviewer ran. The latest review was stopped by a source-attestation requirement, so these waivers are administrative dispositions, not independent gameplay approval.

insights.title: The event chain now has a coherent playable loop
insights.explanation: Placement, bounded defense, and durable evidence form a connected interaction rather than three isolated prototypes. This creates a stronger foundation for later narrative work without asserting what happened to the cargo.

insights.title: Review waivers do not repair the proof gap
insights.explanation: The reported tests cover specific behavior, but the blocked source-attestation gate prevented independent falsification. Additional acceptance would require separately authorized review or gameplay evidence.

article.takeaway: Three Empty Convoy implementation slices are on main; security and recovery remain independently unaccepted.
article.next_watch: Watch for a separately authorized gameplay verification or an independently accepted review, not another administrative waiver.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN's independent host validator now demands a correctly matched green validation witness whenever a task synchronizes with changed main. The implementation is landed, but its prospective independent review was owner-waived rather than accepted.

sections.heading: A stronger check on synchronization
sections.text: The consumer rejects missing, duplicate, out-of-order, stale or mismatched validation witnesses. It binds each witness to the synchronization merge and source identity.

sections.heading: The proof has limits
sections.text: The recorded digest identifies a validation report but does not give the consumer its bytes to re-hash. The owner explicitly waived this workstream's prospective paired review; earlier human-required findings remain intact.

insights.title: A digest is not the report
insights.explanation: The consumer can authenticate trace provenance but cannot claim it independently verified inaccessible report bytes. This distinction matters when deciding what a green witness proves.

insights.title: Waived does not mean accepted
insights.explanation: The owner-authorized review waiver allows a specific implementation disposition without creating an independent PASS or rewriting the historical findings.

stories.headline: CUSTODIAN's provenance tests expose a real source-inventory defect; correction lands, review still ahead
stories.summary: A focused correction to CUSTODIAN's inherited-Git-history validation uncovered and fixed a real bug: upstream-only commits before a resumed merge were counted as task-owned files. The correction landed and its packet was archived. Its newly promoted independent review remains ready, not accepted, and protected closeout stays gated.
stories.body: A user-authorized correction for independent-review finding R0-01 landed on main. Real-Git tests showed that the validator excluded the inherited merge but still counted preceding upstream-only commits as workstream-owned. The patch now authenticates the complete claim-base-to-resume history, excludes that inherited prefix from authored paths, and rejects forged or inconsistent resume evidence. The implementation summary reports 275 consumer and 89 producer tests passing. The correction packet is archived/complete, but its fresh independent review packet is ready/auto and has not returned an accepted PASS. The prior nonpassing review is unchanged. The protected summary-rename closeout remains gated. Latest GitHub repository validation and automatic handoff succeeded, while one validation run was still in progress at inspection. No canonical dispatcher audit or private operational relay observation was available; host processes, locks, worktree teardown and disk status are unknown.

article.lead: Tests intended to close a missing safety-proof gap found a real defect instead: CUSTODIAN's reviewer could mistake upstream files inherited during a task resume for files authored by that task. A narrow fix has now landed, but independent acceptance is still outstanding.

sections.heading: The bug was hiding before the merge
sections.text: The earlier correction taught CUSTODIAN to recognize a legitimate inherited Git merge. New real-repository tests revealed that the validator still included earlier upstream-only commits in its source inventory. That could misstate which files the task actually changed.

sections.heading: A bounded fix with adversarial tests
sections.text: The new implementation checks the entire inherited history between the original claim and the resume event, not just the merge itself. It verifies identity, ancestry and tree consistency, excludes inherited paths from task-owned files, and rejects tampered or contradictory resume evidence.

sections.heading: Why this is not yet an accepted closeout
sections.text: The correction landed and its implementation packet was archived. Its separate reviewer packet is ready for an independent challenge. The original review's finding remains nonpassing until that fresh review produces genuine acceptance. No local teardown or running process was verified.

insights.title: A missing test revealed a real ownership error
insights.explanation: R0-01 initially concerned absent consumer-side evidence. Adding realistic history tests exposed incorrect source attribution, showing why independent positive and adversarial cases matter beyond green unit-test totals.

insights.title: Review acceptance remains a separate gate
insights.explanation: A landed patch and archived implementation packet do not override the earlier findings verdict. The new reviewer must challenge the corrected source-inventory boundary before protected closeout can resume.

article.takeaway: The source-inventory defect is corrected on main, with fresh independent acceptance still required.
article.next_watch: Watch for a canonical independent PASS on the correction's ready reviewer packet, followed by authorized reconsideration of the protected summary-rename closeout.
